children: Brunei’s annual inflation rate stalled in July 2026, following a more than two-year high of 0.3% in the previous month.
Price growth eased for food and non-alcoholic beverages (1.2% vs 1.5% in June) and furnishings, household equipment, and routine household maintenance (0.3% vs 0.4%).
In addition, costs slipped for clothing and footwear (-3.8% vs 3.5%), while deflation deepened for communication (-3.5% vs -0.2%) and miscellaneous goods and services (-1.0% vs -0.6%).
On the other hand, transport costs rebounded (0.2% vs -0.2%), and inflation edged higher for restaurants and hotels (0.6% vs 0.5%) and recreation and culture (0.7% vs 0.4%).
Prices remained steady for housing and utilities (0.0%), health (0.6%), and education (0.3%).
On a monthly basis, consumer prices fell 0.2%, reversing a 0.2% increase in June.

title: Brunei Inflation Rate Stalls in July
